evidence: Procedure per quality-checks.md:9-11: read instruction.md cold and look for numbered acceptance lists, shall/must spec tables, feature matrices, or a build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list). instruction.md has no list, table, numbered item or heading (grep for list markers, table rows and shall/MUST in 17 lines found nothing). It opens as a person's request: line 1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Requirements are given as user needs in first person: line 3 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who'; line 5 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor'; line 7 'whether I am reading or halfway through a reply, never touch my draft or my cursor'. Design freedom is explicit, not a recipe: line 11 'layout and names are yours', 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'; line 13 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' The only endpoint named is GET /api/health (line 13), which is part of the runtime contract row 4 requires, and the Node.js/Express/SQLite, port, DB_PATH, /app/server.js and seed facts (lines 13-15) are the template's mandated runtime contract written as a prose paragraph, not a file layout or route list. Accounts (line 17) are profile-expected demo credentials (SKILL.md known false positives). Observation, not a defect: /instructions/hireops_rules.md is a structured rules note with tables, bullets and HTTP status codes (e.g. lines 21-23 '401'/'403'/'404', line 78 '409') and says 'Follow them exactly' (line 3); it is framed as the team's own working-rules document referenced by the brief (instruction.md line 11), it explicitly leaves 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages' to the builder (lines 3-5), and it describes product behaviour rather than an implementation recipe. A realistic team would hand a builder such a rules note, so the prompt as a whole still reads as a product ask. Counterexample search: (a) a plausible broken app that could pass because of this row - not applicable; this row grades prompt prose, not app behaviour, and no instruction wording hands the agent a recipe that would let a stub look compliant. (b) a conforming alternative that could fail because of the prompt's form - none found; the brief explicitly leaves layout, names, routes and file layout open, and permits polling/SSE/sockets via the note (hireops_rules.md:123). No runtime measurement is required for this row; missing Oracle/judge runs recorded in raw-evidence-index.json affect other rows, not this one.
